title: Republic of Tajikistan
capsule: Tajikistan declared independence on 9 September 1991 as the Soviet Union dissolved, becoming formally recognised in 1992. It immediately descended into a devastating civil war (1992–1997) between the neo-communist government and an Islamist-democratic opposition, killing an estimated 50,000–100,000 people and displacing hundreds of thousands. President Emomali Rahmon, who consolidated power from 1994, brought the war to a negotiated end under a UN-brokered peace accord in 1997 and has governed the country since, concentrating authority through successive constitutional changes. Tajikistan remains the poorest of the post-Soviet states, heavily dependent on aluminium exports and remittances, and shares a long, contested border with Afghanistan.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Tajikistan's internationally recognised borders are well defined, though the Fergana Valley enclaves and segments of the Kyrgyz and Afghan borders have been disputed or undemarcated in recent decades.
